# Atlas content review sheet

> **Status: REVIEWED.** This sheet shows every player-visible record in [`NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json`](../../NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json), exactly as written there, with the evidence behind it. Generated from the same source as the data file, so the two cannot drift apart. AI research and AI review are not canon acceptance: through NDL-012, only your explicit approval marked records `reviewed`. For the content after 2.0 (patches 2.1–3.56) you waived the per-story acceptance gate on 2026-11-19, so the lead marked it `reviewed` after checking every locator by script against the saved wiki pages and running the lint and host tests ([era-modules.md](era-modules.md)).

How to read it:

- **Main** text is what the main-story view shows. **Optional** text replaces it in the default *main + optional* view, because it includes optional Binding Coil quests that are doable and released by that patch (the [available-content rule](../lore-relationship-atlas.md#research-and-content-rules)).
- Each claim quotes a short locator from the Console Games Wiki transcription of that quest, so you can find it. Patch numbers are when the quest was released, which sets the earliest checkpoint where the claim counts.
- Every source links to its quest page on the Console Games Wiki. The Atlas warns before opening it, because those pages list NPCs by full name and can mention later patches.

## Decisions recorded

The user decided these on 2026-11-14:

1. **Source links: on.** Every citation links to its quest page. The [citation audit](content-evidence.md#citation-safety) found that most quest pages list NPCs by full name ("Warde", and "Leveilleur" from 2.2), so the link opens only behind the Atlas's external-page spoiler warning. Each URL names only the quest itself.
2. **Alisaie as a Scion (R14, optional only): keep.** Its only direct support is the optional *Alisaie's Pledge* journal calling her "the young Scion" (C30).
3. **Alphinaud as Louisoix's grandchild (R13, optional, from 2.55): keep.** It rests on two optional lines read together: Louisoix was Alisaie's grandsire (C13, 2.0), and Alphinaud speaks of "our grandsire" shared with his sister (C26, 2.2).

For arc A4 (`NDL-009`), the user decided on 2026-11-14:

4. **The arc:** A4, MSQ #155 *Escape from Castrum Centri* to #161 *The Ultimate Weapon*, with #154 as the baseline ([v2-discovery.md](v2-discovery.md)).
5. **The cast of 10:** Minfilia, Thancred, Alphinaud and the Scions (already in the Atlas); Cid, Gaius, Livia, Lahabrea and the Eorzean Alliance (new); and the Operation Archon event. The plan's caps were raised by one each: five new entities instead of four, and four new relationship types instead of three (*part of*, *prisoner of*, *possessed by*, *serves*).

Lead decisions, confirmed by the user with the content on 2026-11-14:

6. **First names only**, as in the pilot: Gaius, Livia, Cid. Cid's company is "the Ironworks", never its full name.
7. **Slice steps name only the cast.** Text at #154–160 never names a character the slice doesn't cover (such as Tataru or Y'shtola), because the leak sweep can't tell "met before #154" from "not met yet". Raubahn and Rhitahtyn, who are not Atlas entries, are named only from the quest where they appear.
8. **Current quest versions.** Patch 6.1 reworked *Operation Archon* and *The Ultimate Weapon* (the Lahabrea fight became a solo duty). The wiki transcribes the current versions, which is what a player sees today, so the evidence follows them.
9. **Lahabrea is never written as dead,** and Nero is left out: the 2.0 finale shows neither's end. Livia is written as dead, from Cid's "May her soul know rest" (K62).
10. **The arc's name, *The Black Wolf's Challenge*.** It reveals nothing past its first step: by the end of #155 the Black Wolf's ultimatum is already being debated (K26). It avoids reusing #156's quest title, *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum*.

For A Realm Reborn 2.0 before the Black Wolf (`NDL-012`), the user chose the scope on 2026-11-17 (MSQ #102–#154, with the step bound raised). The lead decided the rest, and it awaits your review; the reasoning is in [ndl-012-discovery.md](ndl-012-discovery.md#decisions-to-review):

11. **Five arcs**: *The Road to Titan* (#103–105), *The Fall of the Waking Sands* (#106–110), *The Search for the Enterprise* (#110–129, sharing #110 with the arc before), *Garuda's Barrier* (#130–141) and *The Road to Castrum Centri* (#142–154, stopping before #155 so the Black Wolf's Challenge stays the default there).
12. **The step bound rises from 16 to 128**: one step per main-scenario quest, both #150 paths included, ordered by MSQ index and then authored order.
13. **Marques is his own entry, with no portrait**, because Cid's portrait shows his later look. From #110 he is *revealed as* Cid, and Cid is searchable as "Marques".
14. **Rule 7 above is relaxed**: with #102–#160 covered, text names any entry that is already visible. The leak tests still forbid any name that isn't visible yet, and any later quest title (so the arcs are not named after #105's or #141's quests).
15. **Left out**, as before: Nero, and surnames. The Company of Heroes holds a "feast", because "banquet" is reserved for the 2.55 story.

## Arcs

### The Road to Titan (`arc-b1-road-to-titan`)

From #103 *After In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *After Lord of Crags*. MSQ #103 *In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *Lord of Crags*, with #102 as the baseline (the first timeline step). The Company of Heroes' test, Riol's secret and Titan's fall, ending with the first sight of Lahabrea beside imperial officers (E105e, K14). The Titan storyline starts before #102; the Atlas does not cover those quests.

</details>

**#106–#141 · main**

> Leader of the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, who has the Echo. When imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, she offered to surrender if the innocents were spared. Livia refused, and took her prisoner, wanting her for the Echo.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E106d** Minfilia offered to surrender if the innocents were spared. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "I surrender myself, on the condition you spare the innocents."
  - **K01** Imperial forces led by Livia raid the Waking Sands, refuse Minfilia's surrender and take her prisoner. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "Conditions of surrender...denied. … We leave! Bring the prisoners."
  - **K02** Livia wants Minfilia for the Echo. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "They say she also possesses the Echo. I cannot wait to hear her scream."

**#156–#160 · main**

**#162 only · main** · Also searchable as: the Antecedent

> Leader of the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, who has the Echo. Since the Scions defeated Gaius, patrons crowd her door, and she is torn between their offers and the neutrality she holds fundamental. When Alphinaud urged a move out of Ul'dah to Mor Dhona, she called the idea reckless and dismissed him.

Sources shown: The Scions of the Seventh Dawn — main scenario quest (2.0); The Price of Principles — main scenario quest (2.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C01** Minfilia leads the Scions. *The Scions of the Seventh Dawn* (2.0, main): "My name is Minfilia, and I lead the Scions of the Seventh Dawn."
  - **C33** Minfilia has the Echo. *The Scions of the Seventh Dawn* (2.0, main): "That's right. I too possess the Echo."
  - **M162b** Since the Scions defeated Gaius and destroyed his weapon, the whole world watches them. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Ever since we defeated Gaius van Baelsar and destroyed his ultimate weapon, the eyes of the world have followed our every move"
  - **M162a** Minfilia holds that the Scions' neutrality is fundamental to their cause. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our neutrality is fundamental to our cause."
  - **M162f** Alphinaud proposes moving the Scions' headquarters to Mor Dhona, beyond the great nations' borders. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Alphinaud seizes the opportunity to make a bold counter-proposal: move the Scions' headquarters to [[Mor Dhona]], beyond the borders of [[Ul'dah]] and the other great nations."
  - **M162h** Minfilia calls Alphinaud's idea reckless and dismisses him. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "decrying his idea as reckless beyond words before unceremoniously dismissing him."

</details>

**#163 only · main** · Also searchable as: the Antecedent

> Leader of the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, who has the Echo. She will not hear of leaving Ul'dah, and Alphinaud believes she still hopes her adoptive mother, F'lhaminn, the Songstress of Ul'dah, survived the Calamity. F'lhaminn is alive, and means to reveal herself when the time is right.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C01** Minfilia leads the Scions. *The Scions of the Seventh Dawn* (2.0, main): "My name is Minfilia, and I lead the Scions of the Seventh Dawn."

  - **M163b** Minfilia's adoptive mother, F'lhaminn, the Songstress of Ul'dah, was believed to have died in the Calamity. *Moving On* (2.1, main): "Minfilia's mother─well, adoptive mother─was among the great many who perished during the Calamity. … F'lhaminn was her name, though you may know her better as the “Songstress of Ul'dah.”"

### Alisaie (`char-alisaie`, character)

**2.0–#240 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister. She doubts her brother's approach and has set out to find her own way to heal the realm's troubles. Alphinaud says that although she walks her own path, the twins share the same goal.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C42** The twins call themselves students of history; Alisaie means to find another way to heal the realm. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "You might call us students of history … There must be another way to cure what ails this world─and I mean to find it!"
  - **C11** Alisaie walks her own path, but shares her brother's goal. *Back from the Wood* (2.0, main): "Alisaie has chosen to walk her own path─stubborn girl─but you may be assured that our destination remains the same."

</details>

**2.0–#240 · optional**

**#361–#362 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, who long ago parted from him to walk her own path. She shadowed the Warriors of Darkness until Thancred rescued her; struck by a poisoned arrow, she reached Ishgard near death, warning that Garuda would soon be summoned in Xelphatol.

Sources shown: Promises Kept — main scenario quest (3.4)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M361c** The wounded maiden is Alisaie, Alphinaud's twin, who long ago parted from her brother. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "The maiden is revealed to be none other than [[Alisaie]], [[Alphinaud]]'s twin sister, who had long ago decided to part ways with her brother."
  - **M361d** Thancred, tracking the Warriors of Darkness, found Alisaie on their trail too. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "Thancred explains that after tracking the [[Warriors of Darkness]] for some time, he discovered that she too had attempted to learn more of the enigmatic adventurers."
  - **M361e** Alisaie, struck by a poisoned arrow, is near death. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "Struck by a poisoned arrow as they fled, Alisaie now teeters on the brink of death"
  - **M361f** Alisaie warns that Garuda will soon be summoned in Xelphatol, to be slain by the Warriors of Darkness. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "she musters the strength to warn you of [[Garuda]]'s imminent summoning in [[Xelphatol]]—and of the [[primal]]'s planned death at the hands of the Warriors of Darkness."

</details>

**#242–#243 · main**

> An order devoted to preserving Eorzea's future. Betrayed by the Crystal Braves, its members were condemned as murderers and scattered; you alone escaped Ul'dah to rejoin Alphinaud. Now you, Alphinaud and Tataru are wards of House Fortemps in Ishgard, with Fortemps Manor as your headquarters.

### Alphinaud's trial company (`org-crystal-braves`, organization)

**#196–#198 · main**

> A trial company Alphinaud is raising as a first step toward a realm-wide Grand Company, under Minfilia's authority to ease fears of misuse. Riol, once of the Company of Heroes, and Laurentius are among its recruits. The sultana has blessed it, and much of its funding came from the Syndicate.

Sources shown: Recruiting the Realm — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M196a** Alphinaud plans a realm-wide Grand Company. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "Alphinaud lays before you the plan to establish a realm-wide [[Grand Company]]."
  - **M196b** The trial company is placed under the Antecedent's authority to ease fears of misuse. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "I mean to assuage fears of its misuse by placing the fledgling organization under the authority of the Antecedent."
  - **M196c** Riol, once of the Company of Heroes, joins. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "a member of the now defunct [[Company of Heroes]]."

### The Black Wolf's Challenge (`evt-black-wolfs-challenge`, event)

**#155 only · main**

> You and Cid's crew broke into Castrum Centri and freed Minfilia and the captive Scions, but the escape revealed that the Ascian Lahabrea has possessed Thancred. The Empire has finished the Ultima Weapon, an ancient Allagan relic, and Gaius, the Black Wolf, has given Eorzea's leaders an ultimatum: submit to his power, or share the primals' fate.

Sources shown: Escape from Castrum Centri — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **K20** The rescue party frees the captives held in Castrum Centri's storage tower. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "and the others are being held within the storage tower. … Though the rescue mission was a success"
  - **K21** Cid and Alphinaud create a diversion outside the castrum. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "Alphinaud and I will create a diversion out here and keep them occupied for as long as we are able."
  - **C37** The rescue from Castrum Centri succeeds, and Thancred is revealed to have been possessed by Lahabrea. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "Though the rescue mission was a success, the shocking revelation that Thancred has been possessed by Lahabrea"
  - **K23** The Empire has finished the Ultima Weapon, an Allagan relic excavated beneath Ala Mhigo. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "They finished it. Ultima Weapon... … It is a relic of ancient Allag, excavated from its resting place deep beneath Ala Mhigo."
  - **K25** Gaius demands the realm submit to his power; resistance means sharing the primals' fate. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "This realm founders for want of a ruler with true power─the power to cast down eikons. … Yet offer resistance, and he swears that we shall share the primals' fate."
  - **K26** The Alliance leaders had believed the Scions dead or missing, and now weigh the Black Wolf's ultimatum. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "The Alliance leaders staked their hopes on the Scions, but now they believe us all dead or missing. … I believe we are all acquainted with the terms of the Black Wolf's ultimatum."

</details>

### The Eorzean Alliance (`org-eorzean-alliance`, organization)

**#155 only · main**

> The alliance of Eorzea's city-states. Its leaders had staked their hopes on the Scions and believed them dead or missing, and they are weighing the Black Wolf's ultimatum.

**#156 only · main**

### The Road to Titan (`evt-road-to-titan`, event)

**#103 only · main**

> The Company of Heroes turned a feast at Costa del Sol into a test, weighing you by deeds rather than reputation. Its five chosen members have judged you a worthy challenger for the primal Titan, and Y'shtola, at your side, warns that the battle has yet to begin. Wheiskaet can tell you how to reach Titan's lair.

Sources shown: In the Company of Heroes — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E103a** The feast was a pretext for the Company of Heroes to judge whether you are worthy to face Titan. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "the banquet preparations were but an excuse for his comrades to evaluate your worthiness to face"

At Revenant's Toll you recruited Glaumunt, who bears a grudge against the Empire and knows the castrum, while Y'shtola and Yda scout it.

Sources shown: Reclamation — main scenario quest (2.0); Casing the Castrum — main scenario quest (2.0); Come-Into-My-Castrum — main scenario quest (2.0)

  - **E148e** Glaumunt will help you. *Come-Into-My-Castrum* (2.0, main): "If his response is any indication, it would seem you can indeed expect his aid."
  - **E148d** Y'shtola and Yda go to scout the stronghold. *Come-Into-My-Castrum* (2.0, main): "Yda and I shall go to reconnoiter Garlean activity at the stronghold."

Sources shown: Hope on the Waves — main scenario quest (4.2); Storm on the Horizon — main scenario quest (4.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M515a** An imperial contingent hunting Yotsuyu prepares to deploy to the Ruby Sea. *Hope on the Waves* (4.2, main): "the imperial contingent charged with finding Yotsuyu is preparing to deploy to the [[The Ruby Sea|Ruby Sea]]."
  - **M517c** Emperor Varis personally sanctioned Asahi's mission and lets him speak with his voice. *Storm on the Horizon* (4.2, main): "Indeed, His Radiance, Emperor Varis zos Galvus personally sanctioned this mission, granting me the authority to speak with his voice."
  - **M517f** Asahi is of the Populares, who speak for the common man. *Storm on the Horizon* (4.2, main): "I am of the Populares, a collective which represents the interests of the common man."
  - **M517g** The Optimates, pure-blooded Garleans, oppose the Populares' reforms. *Storm on the Horizon* (4.2, main): "A collection of pure-blooded Garleans who seek to consolidate their own supremacy: the Optimates."

</details>

### A Home Beyond Ul'dah (`evt-a-home-beyond-uldah`, event)

**#162 only · main**

> Since the Scions defeated Gaius, patrons crowd their door, and Minfilia holds their neutrality fundamental. But every offer of patronage comes with a price, Y'shtola warns that their dealings with the city-states have already worn that neutrality thin, and Alphinaud says the Syndicate will never let them stay independent. He urged a move out of Ul'dah to Mor Dhona; Minfilia called the idea reckless and dismissed him.

Sources shown: The Price of Principles — main scenario quest (2.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M162b** Since the Scions defeated Gaius and destroyed his weapon, the whole world watches them. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Ever since we defeated Gaius van Baelsar and destroyed his ultimate weapon, the eyes of the world have followed our every move"
  - **M162a** Minfilia holds that the Scions' neutrality is fundamental to their cause. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our neutrality is fundamental to our cause."
  - **M162c** Y'shtola warns that the Scions' dealings with the city-states have already weakened their claim to neutrality. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our many dalliances with the city–states have already weakened our claim to neutrality"
  - **M162g** Alphinaud says the Syndicate will not let the Scions stay independent, and is why Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "We have demonstrated our capabilities, and the Syndicate has taken note. They will not suffer our organization to remain independent now. … Surely you realize they are the reason Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte?"
  - **M162f** Alphinaud proposes moving the Scions' headquarters to Mor Dhona, beyond the great nations' borders. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Alphinaud seizes the opportunity to make a bold counter-proposal: move the Scions' headquarters to [[Mor Dhona]], beyond the borders of [[Ul'dah]] and the other great nations."
  - **M162h** Minfilia calls Alphinaud's idea reckless and dismisses him. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "decrying his idea as reckless beyond words before unceremoniously dismissing him."

</details>

**#163 only · main**

**#167 only · main**

> A myth made manifest troubles the Twelveswood: Good King Moggle Mog XII, king of the moogles, has returned after five years. The moogle Kuplo Kopp warned of the threat to his kind. Kan-E-Senna has asked you to drive the king out, but he and his Mogglesguard hide behind magical wards.

  - **M167d** The Elder Seedseer asks you to confront the king and drive him from the forest. *Hail to the King, Kupo* (2.1, main): "Thus do we beseech you, [Forename]─confront Good King Moggle Mog XII and drive him from our midst."
  - **M167e** The Mogglesguard and their liege lord hide behind magical wards. *Hail to the King, Kupo* (2.1, main): "The sanctuary of the Mogglesguard and their liege lord is concealed by magical wards."

### Crystals and Exiles (`evt-crystals-and-exiles`, event)

Meanwhile, travelers from Doma have arrived, seeking an audience with the ruler of these lands.

  - **M172a** The crystal stores of a mining concern in Horizon have been secretly pillaged. *Still Waters* (2.2, main): "During a recent audit, it was discovered that the crystal stores of [[Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern]] have been covertly pillaged."
  - **M172b** Minfilia fears the thief may serve a primal. *Still Waters* (2.2, main): "If there is even a possibility that the thief acts not out of self-interest but in service to a primal, we can ill afford to wait for the Blades to realize their mistake."

  - **M172f** Travelers from Doma seek an audience with the ruler of these lands. *Still Waters* (2.2, main): "Far across the sea, from the land of Doma, have we traveled. We seek audience with the ruler of these lands."

> Teledji orchestrated the refugee riots, perhaps to win Omega, the Allagan weapon in the Carteneau Flats, but Ul'dah is not ready to move against him. Alphinaud is troubled that the Scions were kept from knowing of Omega, and sickened that one man's lust for power caused such chaos. He has taken on a refugee girl's search for her parents, and fears Minfilia is too ambitious. Now Minfilia has called you back: the Twelveswood has taken a turn for the worse.

Sources shown: Revolution — main scenario quest (2.3); Stories We Tell — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M190d** Teledji orchestrated the refugee uprising from the start. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "[[Teledji Adeledji]] is one such man, having orchestrated the refugee uprising from the start."
  - **M190h** Raubahn believes Teledji wants Omega's power to subjugate Ul'dah and Eorzea. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "Power enough to subjugate Ul'dah, like as not, and the rest of Eorzea besides─which is doubtless why Teledji Adeledji yearns to have it."
  - **M190i** Your allies are not yet ready to move against Teledji. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "Yet despite having learned of Teledji Adeledji's schemes, it would seem that your allies are not yet ready to move against him"
  - **M191a** Alphinaud wonders how long the Scions would have been kept from knowing of Omega. *Stories We Tell* (2.3, main): "How long do you think they intended to hide the existence of Omega from the Scions?"
  - **M191b** Alphinaud is sickened that one man's lust for power caused the chaos. *Stories We Tell* (2.3, main): "the thought that all this chaos was the product of one man's lust for power sickens me."
  - **M191c** Alphinaud offers to help the girl search for her parents. *Stories We Tell* (2.3, main): "Although he clearly has no desire to do so, Alphinaud offers to assist the girl with her search."
  - **M191d** Alphinaud fears Minfilia is too ambitious. *Stories We Tell* (2.3, main): "Sometimes I fear Minfilia is too ambitious."
  - **M191e** Minfilia calls you back: the Twelveswood has taken a turn for the worse. *Stories We Tell* (2.3, main): "The situation in the Twelveswood has taken a turn for the worse."

</details>

**#192 only · main**

> The sylphs of the Twelveswood are believed to have summoned their guardian, the primal Ramuh. Papalymo thinks the flood of refugees looked to them like another invasion; they first summoned Ramuh after the Calamity, when the Garleans came through the forest. Yda expected it, though not so soon. Ramuh is no raging avatar, so the Elder Seedseer has asked you to treat with him for Gridania, though Minfilia warns it may not go amicably.

Sources shown: Lord of Levin — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M192a** The Twin Adder believes the sylphs have summoned their guardian, the primal Ramuh. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "They have reason to believe that the sylphs may have called forth their revered guardian─the primal Ramuh."
  - **M192d** Papalymo thinks the refugee influx alarmed the sylphs into hastening the summoning. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "'Tis like that the sylphs perceived this panicked migration as yet another invasion, and quickened their efforts to summon their god."
  - **M192e** The sylphs first summoned Ramuh after the Calamity, when the Garleans came through the forest. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "They already summoned Ramuh once right after the Calamity, but that was because the Garleans came tramping through the forest..."
  - **M192c** Yda expected the summoning, just not so soon. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "Oh, it didn't. I was pretty sure it was going to happen─just not this soon."
  - **M192g** Ramuh is no raging avatar of destruction. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "Unlike the other primals you have encountered, Lord Ramuh is no raging avatar of destruction."
  - **M192f** The Elder Seedseer asks you to represent Gridania in a negotiation with Ramuh. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "I would ask therefore that you represent us in this most delicate of negotiations."
  - **M192h** Minfilia warns the meeting may not be amicable. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "Steel yourself for the worst. While I hope for a peaceful resolution to this matter, experience suggests that your meeting with the Lord of Levin will prove less than amicable."

</details>

**#193 only · main**

> The sylphs of the Twelveswood are believed to have summoned their guardian, the primal Ramuh. In the Sylphlands Ramuh declared that the sylphs turned to him for succor, and pronounced sentence on humankind. You defeated him, and he judged you a worthy champion, charging you to excise the sin rooted in man's heart; he sees more in you than the Bringer of Light. Watching the fight, Urianger glimpsed a possible chink in the Ascians' armor.

  - **M193a** Ramuh says the sylphs turned to him for succor, and pronounces sentence on humankind. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "Thus did they turn to me for succor. The sentence I pronounce upon thy kind is just."
  - **M193c** You defeat Ramuh and earn the right to champion peace in the Black Shroud. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "You have defeated the Lord of Levin, and thus earned the right to champion the cause of peace in [[the Black Shroud]]."
  - **M193d** Ramuh judges you a worthy champion and charges you with excising the sin in man's heart. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "And I judge thee a worthy champion. The task of excising the sin that hath taken root in man's heart is thine."
  - **M193b** Ramuh sees something more in you than the Bringer of Light. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "Thou standest apart from thy kin. Thou art the Bringer of Light, aye...but there is something more in thee..."
  - **M193e** Urianger glimpses a possible chink in the Ascians' armor. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "If I mistake not, it may yet prove a chink in the eternal armor of the Ascians."

**#194 onward · main**

> You defeated Ramuh, who judged humankind, and the Elder Seedseer fears his charge strikes home: the Alliance strains under self-interest. The Scions now see why Ascians endure: physical destruction merely inconveniences them, and a Crystal of Darkness, like the one that bound Thancred, may be their way out. With no way to trap one, Urianger has gone to Sharlayan. The Ascians gather: Elidibus speaks of forging a final key, and Lahabrea of the one true god's return.

Sources shown: Levin an Impression — main scenario quest (2.3); What Little Gods Are Made Of — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M193c** You defeat Ramuh and earn the right to champion peace in the Black Shroud. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "You have defeated the Lord of Levin, and thus earned the right to champion the cause of peace in [[the Black Shroud]]."
  - **M194a** The Elder Seedseer sees the Alliance straining under self-interest. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "Our shared struggle against the Empire should have served to seal our union, yet the ties which bind the Alliance strain under the weight of gross self-interest."
  - **M194c** To the Ascians, physical destruction is only a temporary inconvenience. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "that the Ascians are eternal beings, to whom physical destruction is as a temporary inconvenience."
  - **M194e** A Crystal of Darkness, used to control Thancred, may be a gateway to that place. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "The Ascians took control of Thancred by means of a Crystal of Darkness─an artifact which, if our theories are correct, serves as a gateway to the place I have just described."
  - **M194f** The Scions lack a way to trap and destroy an Ascian soul. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "At present, we lack a viable means to entrap and extinguish an Ascian soul."
  - **M194g** Urianger departs to confer with the sages of Sharlayan. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "I will depart at once to convene with the sages of Sharlayan."
  - **M194h** Elidibus says the gifted must be nurtured to forge the final key. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "All that remains is to nurture the strength of the gifted─to forge the final key."
  - **M194i** Lahabrea says the one true god shall come again. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "That which was shattered shall be made anew...and the one true god shall come again."

</details>

### A Company for All Eorzea (`evt-a-company-for-all-eorzea`, event)

**#195 only · main**

> A letter of thanks from the Alliance names every primal you have defeated, from Ifrit to Ramuh. Minfilia expects the Ascians to sow chaos until they are stopped. Alphinaud, who has sought to understand why his grandfather gave his life, wants a new organization that works beyond nations and borders, and vows to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea himself.

  - **M195b** It names every defeated primal, ending with Ramuh. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "It mentions, in particular, the names of all of the defeated primals─Ifrit, Titan, Garuda, Good King Moggle Mog XII, Leviathan, and now Ramuh."
  - **M195c** Minfilia expects the Ascians to sow chaos until they are stopped. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "The Ascians may be relied upon to sow chaos in this realm until such time as they are forced to stop."
  - **M195d** Alphinaud wants a new organization that works beyond nations and borders. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "is a new, expanded organization that operates beyond the limitations of nations and borders."
  - **M195e** Alphinaud sought to understand why his grandfather gave his life. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "I sought to grasp the reason why Grandfather willingly sacrificed himself to protect it."
  - **M195f** Alphinaud vows to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "I, too, will endeavor to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea, and champion these people who toil towards a better world."

</details>

Sources shown: In Pursuit of the Past — main scenario quest (2.0); On the Properties of Primals — main scenario quest (2.1); Build on the Stone — main scenario quest (2.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **K13** Lahabrea is an Ascian. *In Pursuit of the Past* (2.0, main): "the [[Ascian]] uses his magicks to awaken the dragon"
  - **M169f** Minfilia concludes that Ascians were behind both of the king's appearances. *On the Properties of Primals* (2.1, main): "she too is forced to conclude that Ascians were behind both of Good King Moggle Mog XII's recent appearances."
  - **M171f** Minfilia believes Lahabrea endures and may return. *Build on the Stone* (2.1, main): "But I was wrong. He endures, and may yet return."
  - **M171h** Another Ascian says their plans are in motion and Elidibus's intentions unclear. *Build on the Stone* (2.1, main): "We question. Our plans are in motion, your intentions unclear."

</details>

> With Alphinaud you met Ser Aymeric, lord commander of Ishgard's Temple Knights, at Camp Dragonhead. The Holy See will not rejoin the Eorzean Alliance, but Aymeric will keep House Fortemps' aid flowing to Revenant's Toll if the Scions help watch the remains of Midgardsormr, whose return Ishgard's astrologians foretell. Then word came that Iceheart and her heretics had waylaid the latest shipment. Meanwhile Captain Ilberd hunts the Ivy, a Garlean spy in the Immortal Flames.

  - **M202c** Ishgard's astrologians foretell Midgardsormr's return, and Aymeric wants the Scions to help watch the great wyrm's remains. *Coming to Terms* (2.4, main): "You learn that the [[astrologian]]s of Ishgard have foretold the return of [[Midgardsormr]]─the fallen guardian of [[Silvertear Falls]]─and that Ser Aymeric wishes to enlist [[the Scions]]' aid in keeping watch over the great wyrm's remains."
  - **M202e** Iceheart and her followers waylay the latest shipment. *Coming to Terms* (2.4, main): "only to learn moments after that the latest shipment has been waylaid by [[Iceheart]] and her followers..."

### A Blade for the Ascians (`evt-blade-for-the-ascians`, event)

**#218 only · main**

> The Scions want an aetherial blade that can destroy an Ascian's soul, but Moenbryda and Urianger still cannot form one at will, and Minfilia knows Shiva will not be the last primal. Alphinaud is staying in Ul'dah, where his Crystal Braves support the Immortal Flames, shaken by the spy found among their officers. Riol traced a large weapons purchase to a black marketeer, and you are to meet Captain Ilberd at Highbridge to stop the deal.

Sources shown: Good Intentions — main scenario quest (2.5)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M218c** How to form an aetherial blade at will remains unsolved. *Good Intentions* (2.5, main): "Alas, the key problem─how to form an aetherial blade at will─remains unsolved."
  - **M218b** Shiva will not be the last primal, and ties with Ishgard are tenuous. *Good Intentions* (2.5, main): "We both know full well that Saint Shiva will not be the last primal we face...and our relationship with Ishgard is still tenuous at best."
  - **M218a** The Immortal Flames struggle after one of their highest-ranking officers proved a Garlean agent. *Good Intentions* (2.5, main): "As expected, the Immortal Flames have been struggling to cope with the revelation that one of their highest-ranking officers was a Garlean agent."
  - **M218d** Riol, tracing weapons used by disgruntled refugees, learns of a large shipment. *Good Intentions* (2.5, main): "Riol, who has been attempting to trace the source of some weapons wielded by disgruntled refugees, has learned of a large shipment which may be intended for the same purpose."
  - **M218e** Alphinaud sends you to meet Captain Ilberd at Highbridge. *Good Intentions* (2.5, main): "Then it is settled. Rendezvous with Captain Ilberd at Highbridge and intervene when the exchange takes place."

</details>

After Nidhogg's fall he abolished the archbishops' thousand-year rule, and Ishgard is now governed by a House of Commons and a House of Lords. He would have laid down the reins of state, but was elected to the Lords' highest seat. Estinien has disappeared, and Aymeric has asked you to carry him a message.

Sources shown: Litany of Peace — main scenario quest (3.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M360a** Aymeric abolishes the archbishops' thousand-year rule, opening the way to a republic. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "Echoing Estinien's resolve, Ser Aymeric finally moves to abolish the thousand-year rule of the archbishops, paving the way for a new republic."
  - **M360b** Ishgard is now governed by a House of Commons and a House of Lords, and Aymeric is elected to the Lords' highest seat. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "[[Ishgard]]'s governance is placed in the hands of a newly formed House of Commons and House of Lords. And though Ser Aymeric would like nothing more than to lay down the reins of state, he soon finds himself elected to the highest seat in the latter."
  - **M360e** Aymeric and Estinien were the only survivors of a company a dragon attacked. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "our company was set upon by a dragon, and we were the only two to survive."
  - **M360f** Estinien has disappeared, and Aymeric asks you to carry him a message. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "He then reveals that Estinien has disappeared, and asks that you give him a message should your paths ever chance to cross."

</details>

**#224–#240 · main**

> An Ascian. Your lost blessing of Light had kept his kind out of the Scions' domain.   - **M224d** Nabriales escapes through a rift with Minfilia and the relic. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "He then tears open a dimensional rift, through which he escapes with both Minfilia and the relic she holds."
  - **M224g** Minfilia traps the weakened Ascian's soul in white auracite. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Minfilia succeeds in trapping the soul of the weakened Ascian within the chunk of [[White Auracite|white auracite]]."
  - **M224h** Moenbryda spends her own life energy so your blade can pierce Nabriales. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "The wounded scholar then expends her own life energy in a brilliant burst of aether, allowing your glowing blade to at last pierce Nabriales's essence."

### Wards of House Fortemps (`evt-wards-of-house-fortemps`, event)

**#242 only · main**

> Branded murderers after the Crystal Braves turned on you at the victory banquet, you escaped Ul'dah alone while your comrades stayed behind, and rejoined Alphinaud in Coerthas. Now Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps, which opens Ishgard's gates. Haurchefant offers Fortemps Manor as your new headquarters, where any missing allies will be welcome. Ishgard, ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII, has been at war for a thousand years and keeps its borders closed.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242e** The Scions, betrayed by the Crystal Braves, fled the victory banquet and are condemned as murderers. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "are now condemned as murderers─betrayed by the [[Crystal Braves]] and forced to flee the banquet held to celebrate the very victory"
  - **M242f** Your comrades stayed behind one by one, and you alone escaped to rejoin Alphinaud and take refuge in Coerthas. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "until you alone emerged from the tunnels beneath [[Ul'dah]] to be reunited with Alphinaud and seek refuge in [[Coerthas]]"
  - **M242a** Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Count Edmont has decreed that the three of you be taken in as wards of House Fortemps."
  - **M242b** Haurchefant offers the family manor as the Scions' new headquarters. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Pray consider our manor your new headquarters"
  - **M242g** Haurchefant says any missing allies who are found will be welcome at the manor. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "should any of your missing allies be found─as I am certain they shall─they will of course be welcome to join you there."
  - **M242c** Ishgard is devoted to Halone and ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A great and proud nation devoted to Halone, the Fury, ruled by Thordan VII, Archbishop of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church..."
  - **M242d** After a thousand years of war, Ishgard had forgotten peace. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A land that after a thousand years of war had forgotten what it was to be at peace."

</details>

**#244 only · main**

> Branded murderers after the Crystal Braves' betrayal, you, Alphinaud and Tataru are wards of House Fortemps, which has taken a great risk in sheltering you. The lowborn Brume bore the worst of a wyvern attack, and Ser Aymeric's knights are strengthening the defenses. Count Edmont accepted the Scions' help and set you to aid his sons, Artoirel and Emmanellain, who greeted the offer with indignation and mirth. Tataru stays at a tavern to gather news of the missing Scions.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0); The Better Half — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242e** The Scions, betrayed by the Crystal Braves, fled the victory banquet and are condemned as murderers. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "are now condemned as murderers─betrayed by the [[Crystal Braves]] and forced to flee the banquet held to celebrate the very victory"

  - **M244a** The Brume suffered worst in the wyvern attack, while the Pillars had the High Houses and Temple Knights to protect them. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "it was the Brume that got the worst of it, while the Pillars enjoyed the protection of the High Houses and the Temple Knights."
  - **M244b** Ser Aymeric has ordered his knights to strengthen Ishgard's defenses, and every house is asked to help. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "Ser Aymeric has ordered his knights to strengthen our defenses, and each house has been called upon to lend what support it can."
  - **M244c** Edmont accepts the Scions' help, hoping to secure provisions from abroad. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "Such qualities may prove most useful to us in our efforts to secure provisions from foreign sources"
  - **M244d** Edmont asks you to help his sons, Artoirel and Emmanellain, with their duties. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "to aid Artoirel and Emmanellain in their duties."
  - **M244e** Edmont's two sons greet the offer with indignation and mirth. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "unlike his two sons, who greet your proposal with a mixture of indignation and mirth."
  - **M244g** Tataru stays at the Forgotten Knight tavern to gather news, perhaps of the missing Scions. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "[[Tataru]] proposes that she stay behind and ingratiate herself with the regulars."

</details>

### The Sea of Clouds (`evt-the-sea-of-clouds`, event)

**#245b only · main**

> You, Alphinaud and Tataru are wards of House Fortemps in Ishgard, and Count Edmont has set you to help his sons. His second son, Emmanellain, who longs to escape his brother's shadow, took you to Camp Cloudtop in the Sea of Clouds to aid House Haillenarte. Its commander, Ser Laniaitte, is the elder sister of Francel, whom you once saved, and thinks little of Emmanellain. Her airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by clashes with the Vanu Vanu.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0); The Better Half — main scenario quest (3.0); Onwards and Upwards — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242a** Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Count Edmont has decreed that the three of you be taken in as wards of House Fortemps."
  - **M244d** Edmont asks you to help his sons, Artoirel and Emmanellain, with their duties. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "to aid Artoirel and Emmanellain in their duties."
  - **M245ba** Emmanellain, Edmont's second son, longs to escape his elder brother's shadow. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "has long dreamed of emerging from beneath his elder brother's shadow"
  - **M245bc** Emmanellain's mission is to aid House Haillenarte. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "we are to aid the good men and women of House Haillenarte."
  - **M245bd** Camp Cloudtop was built to warn of Dravanian incursions. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Camp Cloudtop was established to provide early warning of impending Dravanian incursions."
  - **M245be** Ser Laniaitte of House Haillenarte commands Camp Cloudtop. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "I am Ser Laniaitte de Haillenarte, commander of the forces stationed here at Camp Cloudtop."
  - **M245bg** Laniaitte is the elder sister of Francel, whose unjust execution you prevented. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Lady Laniaitte explains that she is the elder sister of Lord [[Francel]], whose unjust execution you prevented during your search for the ''Enterprise'' long ago."
  - **M245bh** Laniaitte thinks little of Emmanellain, who does not notice. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "though the young lord seems oblivious to her low opinion of him."
  - **M245bf** The camp's great airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by skirmishes with the Vanu Vanu. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "our efforts have been hampered by an indigenous beast tribe known as the Vanu Vanu, with whom we have had several skirmishes already."

</details>

### Friends in Chains (`evt-friends-in-chains`, event)

**#259 only · main**

> Count Edmont had only begun to thank you for your work at Falcon's Nest and Camp Cloudtop when word came that Ser Grinnaux of the Heavens' Ward, the archbishop's personal guard, had arrested Alphinaud and Tataru for heresy. The lord commander, Ser Aymeric, believed them innocent but could not overrule the Ward, and Edmont suspects a plot by House Dzemael against House Fortemps. You won the trial by combat that the law demanded, and your friends went free.

Sources shown: Divine Intervention — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

Anyway, we've been studying their trail of destruction, hoping it might lead us somewhere—which it has singularly failed to do."

### Gosetsu (`char-gosetsu`, character)

**#377–3.56 · main**

> A Doman warrior who came to Eorzea with word that his master is in peril and Doma calls Yugiri home; Urianger found him collapsed in the street. When Yugiri chose to stay and face the crisis, he joined the Omega expedition, his blade oathbound against the imperials.

Sources shown: The Greater Obeisance — main scenario quest (3.56)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M377b** Gosetsu brings word that his master is in peril and Doma calls Yugiri home. *The Greater Obeisance* (3.56, main): "Our master languishes in dire peril, and Doma calls her daughter home!"
  - **M377c** Urianger came to Gosetsu's aid when he collapsed. *The Greater Obeisance* (3.56, main): "Collapsed in the street like an unfed stray, I was, until Lord Urianger came to my aid."
  - **M377e** Yugiri stays to play her part in the crisis. *The Greater Obeisance* (3.56, main): "A crisis threatens all within this realm, Eorzean and Doman alike, and I go to play my part in its resolution."
  - **M377f** Gosetsu's blade is oathbound against the imperials. *The Greater Obeisance* (3.56, main): "My blade is oathbound to fall upon the ranks of the imperials wheresoever they march!"

</details>

**#380–#412 · main**

> A Doman warrior returning with Yugiri to their master and their home, Doma, to fight Garlemald. He says their purpose and the Scions' are one, though their battlefields lie far apart.

Sources shown: Beyond the Great Wall — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M380d** Yugiri and Gosetsu return to Doma to aid their comrades against Garlemald. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "The pair have resolved to return to the nation of [[Doma]], in the Far East, to aid their comrades in the fight against Garlemald."
  - **M380p** Gosetsu says the Domans' purpose and the Scions' are one, though their battlefields lie far apart. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "Though our battlefields be a thousand malms apart, our purpose is one!"
  - **M380r** Yugiri's people have a new home and no longer need her; she and Gosetsu return to their master. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "They have built a new home for themselves, and lo longer need me to shepherd them. The time has come for Gosetsu and I to return to our master—to our home."

</details>

**#416–#418 · main**

> A Doman samurai, sworn with Yugiri to Lord Hien, heir to Doma's throne. He stood by Hien in their doomed war until they were separated in battle, then parted from Yugiri to search for him. Freed in Kugane, he joins the Scions to lead them to Yugiri.

### Lyse (`char-lyse`, character)

**3.56 only · main** · Also searchable as: Yda

> The Scion you knew as Yda: Yda's younger sister, who served for years in her mask and name. Yda died six years ago smuggling refugees out of Ala Mhigo; Papalymo brought Lyse her mask as a keepsake, she chose to carry on her sister's work, and Papalymo persuaded those who knew to keep the secret. Their father fought to overthrow Ala Mhigo's mad king, and now she means to continue her family's fight for Ala Mhigo.

Sources shown: The Far Edge of Fate — main scenario quest (3.56)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M379g** Yda is not Yda: she is Lyse, the fallen Archon's younger sister. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "revealing at last that she is not Yda at all, but the fallen [[Archon]]'s younger sister, [[Lyse]]."
  - **M379h** Her real name is Lyse. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "I'm sorry for lying to you. My real name is Lyse."
  - **M379i** Yda died six years ago smuggling refugees out of Ala Mhigo. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "Yda died six years ago, on a mission to smuggle refugees out of Ala Mhigo."
  - **M379j** Papalymo brought Lyse Yda's mask as a keepsake, and she chose to take up her sister's work. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "When Papalymo brought me Yda's mask, it was meant as a keepsake. But I decided I wanted to be his new partner; to keep alive all the good that she had done."
  - **M379k** Papalymo persuaded the others to keep up the charade. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "'Twas Papalymo who persuaded us to maintain the charade."
  - **M379m** Their father fought to overthrow the mad king Theodoric. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "He had fought to overthrow the mad king, Theodoric."
  - **M379l** Lyse will continue her family's fight for Ala Mhigo. *The Far Edge of Fate* (3.56, main): "...And I choose to continue my family's fight."

</details>

  - **M384c** The Resistance is more fragmented than the Scions realize. *A Bargain Struck* (4.0, main): "But the Resistance is far more fragmented than you realize."
  - **M384d** Trusted veterans died at the Wall, and young recruits fill their posts. *A Bargain Struck* (4.0, main): "Some of our most trusted veterans died at the Wall, and we've had to fill their posts with the young and inexperienced."

**#397–#405 · main**

> The Ala Mhigan Resistance, allied with the Eorzean Alliance through Conrad in Rhalgr's Reach. Together they destroyed imperial prototype weapons at East End without a single casualty, and its ranks are swelling with recruits and with Scions; once they are trained, Conrad will propose an assault on Castellum Velodyna.

Sources shown: A Bargain Struck — main scenario quest (4.0); Best Served with Cold Steel — main scenario quest (4.0); Let Fill Your Hearts with Pride — main scenario quest (4.0); Where Men Go as One — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M384a** Conrad accepts the Eorzean Alliance's proposal. *A Bargain Struck* (4.0, main): "I, Conrad Kemp, do hereby accept the Eorzean Alliance's proposal."
  - **M387c** Grynewaht's weapon is destroyed; he flees, and the Alliance and Resistance celebrate. *Best Served with Cold Steel* (4.0, main): "As the smoldering wreck of his beloved weapon belches smoke into the sky, the imperial officer flees, leaving the combined force of [[Eorzean Alliance|Alliance]] regulars and [[Ala Mhigan Resistance|Resistance]] fighters to celebrate a momentous victory."
  - **M387e** The operation cost no casualties. *Best Served with Cold Steel* (4.0, main): "Not a single casualty, for which I'm grateful beyond words."
  - **M388b** Conrad calls it the beginning of a united Eorzea's campaign to drive out the Garleans. *Let Fill Your Hearts with Pride* (4.0, main): "the beginning of a campaign by a united Eorzea to drive the Garleans from our lands."
  - **M397a** Alphinaud brings Scions eager to join the endeavor with the Resistance. *Where Men Go as One* (4.0, main): "There were several amongst the Scions' ranks that were quite eager to take part in our joint endeavor with the Resistance"
  - **M397e** Once the recruits are trained, Conrad will propose an assault on Castellum Velodyna. *Where Men Go as One* (4.0, main): "Once our new recruits have received sufficient training, I will propose to General Aldynn that we draw up plans for an assault on Castellum Velodyna."

</details>

### The House of Lords (`org-house-of-lords`, organization)

**#360 only · main**

> One of the two houses that, with the House of Commons, now govern Ishgard after the archbishops' rule was abolished. Ser Aymeric was elected to its highest seat.

Sources shown: Litany of Peace — main scenario quest (3.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M360a** Aymeric abolishes the archbishops' thousand-year rule, opening the way to a republic. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "Echoing Estinien's resolve, Ser Aymeric finally moves to abolish the thousand-year rule of the archbishops, paving the way for a new republic."
  - **M360b** Ishgard is now governed by a House of Commons and a House of Lords, and Aymeric is elected to the Lords' highest seat. *Litany of Peace* (3.3, main): "[[Ishgard]]'s governance is placed in the hands of a newly formed House of Commons and House of Lords. And though Ser Aymeric would like nothing more than to lay down the reins of state, he soon finds himself elected to the highest seat in the latter."

### The Lost Scions (`evt-the-lost-scions`, event)

**#336 only · main**

> In Ishgard, Ser Aymeric has taken up the vacant archbishop's duties, and sends Lucia, with you and Alphinaud, to Anyx Trine to restore relations with Hraesvelgr's brood through Vidofnir. Meanwhile the hunt for Minfilia and Thancred is at a standstill, though Riol's men have leads on F'lhaminn, Yda and Papalymo, and a Sharlayan scholar of the Students of Baldesion is coming to help.

Sources shown: An Uncertain Future — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M336a** With the archbishop's seat vacant after his father's passing, Aymeric has assumed its responsibilities under canon law. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "With my father's passing, the seat of the archbishop lies vacant. And so, in accordance with canon law, I have assumed his responsibilities."
  - **M336d** Aymeric sends you to escort Lucia to Anyx Trine to treat with Vidofnir and restore relations with Hraesvelgr's brood. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "Ser Aymeric bids you escort [[Lucia]] to [[Anyx Trine]], that she might treat with [[Vidofnir]] and thereby reestablish diplomatic relations with [[Hraesvelgr]]'s brood."
  - **M336g** The hunt for Minfilia and Thancred is at a standstill. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "the hunt for [[Minfilia Warde|Minfilia]] and [[Thancred]] remains at a standstill."
  - **M336h** Riol's men report that F'lhaminn slipped aboard a ship for Radz-at-Han. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "according to Riol, she crept aboard a ship bound for Radz-at-Han, where she's been hiding ever since."
  - **M336i** Riol thinks Yda and Papalymo threw away their linkpearls after escaping the Royal Promenade. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "Riol thinks they must have disposed of them after escaping from the Royal Promenade."
  - **M336j** A Sharlayan scholar of the Students of Baldesion has been enlisted to help the search. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "we've enlisted the services of a Sharlayan scholar─one of the Students of Baldesion─to aid in the search"

### The Conference at Falcon's Nest (`evt-falcons-nest-conference`, event)

**#346 only · main**

> Ser Aymeric means to make peace with the Dravanians: Vidofnir's rescue of a child gave hope, and he is arranging a peace conference at Falcon's Nest for her to attend, with you there in case Nidhogg, implacably opposed, tries to disrupt it. There Lucia, once a foreign spy who pledged herself to Ishgard, oversees a relief to be unveiled. Alphinaud asks you to keep Minfilia's fate from the others.

Sources shown: This War of Ours — main scenario quest (3.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M346b** Vidofnir's rescue of a child gave hope of peace between man and dragon. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Yet in adversity were we blessed with the promise of peace between man and dragon, through Vidofnir's timely rescue of an innocent child."
  - **M346c** Aymeric is arranging a peace conference at Falcon's Nest, to be attended by Vidofnir. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "he has begun making formal arrangements for a peace conference in [[Falcon's Nest]], to be attended by [[Vidofnir]]"
  - **M346d** Aymeric fears Nidhogg, implacably opposed to peace, may disrupt the conference. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Given Nidhogg's implacable opposition to the peace, it is possible that he and his followers may attempt to disrupt proceedings"
  - **M346e** Lucia was sent to Ishgard as a foreign spy. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Dispatched to a foreign nation as a spy, it was her duty to infiltrate [[Ishgard]]ian society for her masters' ends."
  - **M346f** Lucia chose instead to pledge herself to Ishgard's cause and war. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "In the end, however, she chose a different path—to pledge herself to another nation's cause, and to join in their war."
  - **M346g** A relief at Falcon's Nest will be unveiled during the conference. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "It conceals a relief that will be unveiled during the conference."
  - **M346a** Alphinaud will tell Tataru and Urianger of Minfilia's fate, but asks you to tell no one else, least of all F'lhaminn. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Although [[Alphinaud]] intends to inform [[Tataru]] and [[Urianger]] of [[Minfilia Warde|Minfilia's]] fate, he asks that you share with no one else what you have learned—especially [[F'lhaminn]]."

</details>

### Waking Omega (`evt-waking-omega`, event)

**#376 only · main**

> The primal Ilberd summoned waits in a cocoon of light above the Wall, sealed by Papalymo's sacrifice; a Garlean airship that approached was destroyed. Nero, a former tribunus who studied beside Cid, offered the Alliance council Omega, an Allagan weapon beneath Carteneau, and the council sent Cid's contingent to take command of it. Alphinaud wonders how Nero learned of the meeting.

  - **M410g** Alisaie accepts Hancock's invitation for now. *The Man from Ul'dah* (4.0, main): "I say we accept his invitation—for now."

</details>

**#412–#413 · main**

> Lolorito's trading company, which hosts the Scions in Kugane. Its aid is offered as contrition for the bloody banquet, and its interests coincide with aiding the Doman Liberation Front; Yugiri and Gosetsu reached Kugane on one of its ships.

Sources shown: The Man from Ul'dah — main scenario quest (4.0); By the Grace of Lord Lolorito — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M410c** Hancock of the East Aldenard Trading Company welcomes them on behalf of Chairman Lolorito. *The Man from Ul'dah* (4.0, main): "Hancock, of the East Aldenard Trading Company, at your service. On behalf of Chairman Lolorito, I bid you welcome to Kugane"
  - **M412a** Hancock calls the company's aid Lolorito's contrition for the bloody banquet. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "the chairman bids you consider this as an expression of his heartfelt contrition for the bloody banquet and the unpleasantness which followed."
  - **M412b** The company's interests coincide with aiding the Doman Liberation Front. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "By sheer coincidence, your purpose here happens to coincide with our own interests. That is, assuming you are come to aid the Doman Liberation Front?"
  - **M412c** Yugiri and Gosetsu came on a company vessel but could not cross the Ruby Sea. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "They came here aboard a company vessel, you see. However, they encountered difficulties securing passage across the Ruby Sea."

</details>

**#414 onward · main**

> Lolorito's trading company in Kugane, which hosts the Scions. Through Hancock it has struck an agreement with Soroban, a Kojin merchant who offers the Scions passage across the Ruby Sea.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M414e** Your savior is Soroban, a Kojin of the Blue and a merchant who wants an agreement with Hancock. *It's Probably a Trap* (4.0, main): "at last learn the identity of your savior: Soroban, a Kojin of the Blue. … A merchant by trade, he seeks to broker an agreement with Hancock, who is more than happy to do so."
  - **M414f** Soroban offers passage across the Ruby Sea. *It's Probably a Trap* (4.0, main): "Ah, yes─you sought passage across the Ruby Sea, did you not?"

### The Confederacy (`org-confederacy`, organization)

**#412–#416 · main**

> A maritime collective that has controlled the Ruby Sea since antiquity, demanding the Ruby Tithe in exchange for its fleet's protection. Doma's acting viceroy has condemned it, and Hingashi has cut ties with it and banned the payment.

Sources shown: By the Grace of Lord Lolorito — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M412d** The Ruby Sea belongs to neither Hingashi nor Doma but to the Confederacy. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "the Ruby Sea does not fall within the dominion of either Hingashi or Doma, being controlled since antiquity by a third party: namely, the Confederacy."
  - **M412e** The Confederacy charges every ship in its waters a toll, the Ruby Tithe, for its protection. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "demanding that any vessel entering its waters pay a toll referred to as the"
  - **M412f** Doma's recently appointed acting viceroy has condemned the Confederacy. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "The recently appointed acting imperial viceroy of Doma had other ideas, however. She has formally condemned the Confederacy"
  - **M412g** Hingashi cut ties with the Confederacy and forbade the Ruby Tithe. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "Bowing to this pressure, Hingashi severed ties with these toll-takers and forbade the payment of the Ruby Tithe"

</details>

**#417 only · main**

> The maritime collective that rules the Ruby Sea. Crossing without the Ruby Tithe invites it to claim your vessel, and your life if you resist; paying earns the pirate lords' blessing. Tansui serves its captain.

Sources shown: By the Grace of Lord Lolorito — main scenario quest (4.0); Open Water — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M412d** The Ruby Sea belongs to neither Hingashi nor Doma but to the Confederacy. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "the Ruby Sea does not fall within the dominion of either Hingashi or Doma, being controlled since antiquity by a third party: namely, the Confederacy."
  - **M417a** Setting out unprepared invites the Confederacy to claim your vessel and your life. *Open Water* (4.0, main): "To set forth without making the necessary preparations is to invite the Confederacy to claim your vessel─and your life should you resist."
  - **M417b** Paying the Ruby Tithe earns the pirate lords' blessing. *Open Water* (4.0, main): "But this fate can be avoided by paying the Ruby Tithe, thereby earning you the blessing of the pirate lords."
  - **M417d** Tansui is a mate serving the Confederacy's captain. *Open Water* (4.0, main): "I am Tansui, a humble mate who serves at the pleasure of the Confederacy's captain."

</details>

**#418 only · main**

> The maritime collective that rules the Ruby Sea, many of its members of Doman descent. It will not hinder imperial ships, lest Doma's acting viceroy brand it an enemy of the Empire, but counted the Scions' tithe paid for what it expects of them.

Sources shown: By the Grace of Lord Lolorito — main scenario quest (4.0); Boys with Boats — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M412d** The Ruby Sea belongs to neither Hingashi nor Doma but to the Confederacy. *By the Grace of Lord Lolorito* (4.0, main): "the Ruby Sea does not fall within the dominion of either Hingashi or Doma, being controlled since antiquity by a third party: namely, the Confederacy."
  - **M418c** Tansui counts the Scions' tithe paid for what he expects they will do. *Boys with Boats* (4.0, main): "I shall consider their tithe paid─not for what they have done, but for what I expect they will do."
  - **M418e** Defying the Empire would see the Confederacy branded its enemy. *Boys with Boats* (4.0, main): "she'll accuse us of attempting to foment rebellion and brand us enemies of the Empire"
  - **M418f** Many in the Confederacy are of Doman descent, and the acting viceroy is no friend of Domans. *Boys with Boats* (4.0, main): "many of my comrades in the Confederacy are of Doman descent─and the acting viceroy...well, she's none too fond of Domans, to say the least."
  - **M418h** Tansui says the Confederacy is outmatched by the imperial army. *Boys with Boats* (4.0, main): "Compared to them, we're boys with boats."

**#419 only · main**

> The pirates of the Ruby Sea. Their large settlement on the isle of Onokoro, complete with its own aetheryte, lies near Isari, a village the Empire occupies. Gosetsu sent you to them for aid, though there seems little chance they will answer.

  - **M419i** Gosetsu bade you seek aid at the tower to the northeast. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "Recalling that Gosetsu bade you seek aid at the mysterious tower to the northeast"
  - **M419k** There seems little chance the Confederacy will answer your call. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "there is surely little chance that they will answer your call."

</details>

**#420–#421c · main**

> The pirates of the Ruby Sea, led by their captain, Rasho, from Onokoro. Members renounce every other tie, and the Confederacy is allied with none. It did not defend Doma when the Empire invaded twenty-five years ago, and Rasho refuses to fight the Empire over Isari.

  - **M420d** The Confederacy did not rush to Doma's defense when the Empire invaded twenty-five years ago. *Confederate Consternation* (4.0, main): "When Doma was invaded by the Empire twenty-five years ago, we did not rush to her defense."
  - **M420e** Rasho says hate is a luxury they cannot afford, and refuses further aid. *Confederate Consternation* (4.0, main): "Hate is a luxury we cannot afford.<br>You are free to come and go as you please, but you will receive no further aid."

</details>

### Castrum Oriens (`loc-castrum-oriens`, location)

**#380–#404 · main**

> An imperial castrum by the Wall, at the edge of Gyr Abania, which the Eorzean Alliance occupied after the attack on the Wall and the primal's summoning. From its command center Raubahn holds the Alliance's line, and will not advance into Gyr Abania without the Ala Mhigan Resistance.

**#419 only · main**

> Soroban, a Blue Kojin, carried you to Othard's coast. In Isari, occupied by imperial forces, the viceroy Yotsuyu forced one villager to execute another, and Gosetsu, who calls her a traitor to her homeland, surrendered to her so you could plan his rescue. On his advice, Alisaie and Lyse led you to Onokoro, a large settlement held by the Confederacy.

Sources shown: To Bend with the Wind — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M419a** Soroban, relieved that you will not judge his Blue Kojin for the deeds of the Red, carries you on to Othard. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "Relieved that you will not judge him and his fellow Blue Kojin harshly for the deeds of the Red, Soroban is eager to take you the rest of the way to Othard"
  - **M419b** Isari, a village on Othard's coast, is occupied by imperial forces. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "turn your attentions to Isari, which you soon discover to be occupied by imperial forces"

  - **M419g** Gosetsu calls Yotsuyu the traitor who sold her homelands to the Garleans. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "The traitor who sold her homelands to the Garleans—Yotsuyu!"

> To win the Confederacy's help in freeing Isari, you wagered to deprive the Empire of its Red Kojin allies. **#430 only · main**

> You found the Yasakani-no-Magatama, a sacred Kojin jewel, while seeking a way to draw the Red Kojin away from the imperial garrison in Isari. Bunchin gave you a knife to open the Kojin vault on the Isle of Zekki, which holds the jewel's two siblings: an attack there would pull the Red from their posts. Soroban will ready the Confederacy to strike.

  - **M430c** An attack on the vault would summon Kojin from all around to defend it. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "Were the vault to be attacked, their response would by necessity be immediate. Kojin would be summoned from malms around to defend their treasures."
  - **M430d** Without the Kojin, the imperials lack the troops to hold Isari. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "Without the Kojin, the imperials don't have nearly enough troops in Isari to hold off the pirates."
  - **M430e** Soroban will tell the Confederacy to be ready to act. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "I shall inform the Confederacy of your plans, and bid them make ready to act when the time is right."

### The Silence of Yanxia (`evt-the-silence-of-yanxia`, event)

**#434 only · main**

> With Isari freed, Gosetsu, still hurt from Grynewaht's interrogation, led you into Yanxia. After crushing Doma's rebellion, Zenos left and named Yotsuyu to rule in his stead, and her purges of the villages ended long ago, but their memory keeps the people in line. Elsewhere, Grynewaht defeated the Red Kojin who abandoned their posts.

Sources shown: A Silence in Three Parts — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M434a** Confederate forces drove Yotsuyu from Isari, and the captives survived. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "[[Yotsuyu]] and her imperials have been driven from [[Isari]], and their former captives managed to survive their ordeal."
  - **M434e** Gosetsu is still hurt from Grynewaht's interrogation. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "Despite his assurances, [[Gosetsu]] is clearly still troubled by the injuries he sustained from [[Grynewaht]]'s brutal interrogation."
  - **M434b** Zenos left Doma after crushing the rebellion and named Yotsuyu to serve in his stead. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "[[Zenos]] had no desire to remain in Doma after he crushed the rebellion, and so he named Yotsuyu to serve in his stead."
  - **M434c** The acting viceroy waged an indiscriminate campaign of terror on the villages. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "The acting viceroy waged an indiscriminate campaign of terror, marching into villages without warning"
  - **M434d** The purges ceased, but their memory keeps the people from resisting. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "After a time, these purges ceased, but the memory remains, and with it the promise of punishment should the people resist."
  - **M434f** Grynewaht cuts down the Red Kojin there and destroys most of their treasure. *A Silence in Three Parts* (4.0, main): "''Grynewaht defeats all of the Red Kojin and destroys most of the treasure.''"

</details>

### The Flood at Doma Castle (`evt-the-flood-at-doma-castle`, event)

**#465 only · main**

> With Lord Hien back among his people, Alphinaud has drawn up a plan to retake Doma Castle: diversions by Lyse and the Doman irregulars, a Xaela strike on the castle's airborne defenses, and ships bombarding it as they sail for the enclave. Hien has agreed to it. Alphinaud has sent you to Kugane, where Tataru has taken to Hingan fashion, for Cid's documents on the field generators.

Sources shown: The Room Where It Happened — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M465a** Anticipating Lord Hien's return, Alphinaud has drawn up a plan to retake Doma Castle. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "In anticipation of Lord Hien's return, Alphinaud has developed a comprehensive strategy to retake Doma Castle."
  - **M465b** Lyse and the Doman irregulars will open with diversions, then the Xaela will strike the castle's airborne defenses. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "After Lyse and the Doman irregulars carry out a series of diversionary attacks, the Xaela will launch a surprise attack on the castle's airborne defenses."
  - **M465c** Ships will bombard the castle while sailing west toward the Doman Enclave. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "They will commence to bombard the castle with cannon fire, while sailing west towards the Doman Enclave."
  - **M465g** Hien will carry out Alphinaud's plan to the letter. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "We shall carry out Alphinaud's plan to the letter."
  - **M465f** Tataru has taken after Hancock and dresses in the latest Hingan fashions. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "You are shocked to find Tataru a woman transformed, having taken after Hancock and dressed herself in the latest Hingan fashions."
  - **M465e** Alphinaud doubts he can disable the castle's field generators, so he has turned to Cid. *The Room Where It Happened* (4.0, main): "Alphinaud lacks confidence in his ability to disable the field generators"

</details>

  - **M500b** Pipin receives Tizona. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "By the Twelve, this is... this is Tizona!"
  - **M500c** The wolfmen hail from Doma and were coerced into fighting for the Empire. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "hail from Doma. They were ''coerced'' into fighting for the Empire"
  - **M500d** Doma is free: Lord Hien drove out Yotsuyu and the imperials. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "Doma is free! Lord Hien has returned and driven Yotsuyu and the imperials from your lands."
  - **M500f** Hakuro names himself the White and challenges you. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "I am the White! I am Hakuro! And I will be your opponent! Have at you!"
  - **M500g** Hakuro demands the tale be proved on the battlefield. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "Words are air! You will prove the truth of your tale on the battlefield, or die in dishonor!"
  - **M500h** Hakuro vows to turn on the imperials when the gates are breached. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "When you breach the gates, we shall turn on the imperials as one."
  - **M500i** Hien declares that Doma has come to pay her debts. *The Measure of His Reach* (4.0, main): "Doma is come to pay her debts!"

**4.0 onward · main**

> Hien's forces helped break the gate of Ala Mhigo, and you stormed the palace. On its roof Zenos merged with Shinryu, Ilberd's primal, and after his defeat he took his own life. The rest of his legion surrendered, ending twenty years of occupation, and the people sang. Lyse then left the Scions to serve Ala Mhigo.

Sources shown: Stormblood — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M501a** Allies from the Far East led by Lord Hien swoop in to the rescue at the gate. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "allies, led by Lord [[Hien]], swoop in to the rescue"
  - **M501b** The gate gives way under the renewed assault. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "The gate buckles under the renewed assault, and soon gives way."
  - **M501c** Shinryu, Ilberd's god of vengeance, is at the viceroy's mercy. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "[[Shinryu]], [[Ilberd]]'s draconic god of vengeance, at the mercy of the viceroy."
  - **M501d** Zenos uses his power as a Resonant to merge with the primal and bind it. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "uses his power as a [[Resonant]] to merge with the primal, binding it to his will."
  - **M501f** Zenos takes his own life, at peace, before Lyse can stop him. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "He brings the blade to his neck and smiles the smile of a man at peace, and before Lyse can intervene, the deed is done."
  - **M501k** The rest of the XIIth surrendered, and the twenty-year occupation is ended. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "With their commander fallen, the remainder of the XIIth chose to surrender to our forces. After twenty long years it's official: the occupation is ended."
  - **M501g** The people of Ala Mhigo sing as word of the viceroy's death spreads. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "as the horns spread word of the viceroy's death, the people of Ala Mhigo raise their voices in song"
  - **M501h** Lyse declares she will formally leave the Scions. *Stormblood* (4.0, main): "Lyse declares her intention to formally leave the Scions of the Seventh Dawn."

### Spoils of Liberation (`evt-spoils-of-liberation`, event)

**#502 only · main**

> Ala Mhigo is free but has no leader, and its last king, Theodoric, was called the mad king for good reason. Arenvald has set you and Alphinaud on the trail of the mad king's trove, the wealth Theodoric is said to have hoarded from the kinsmen he executed, which soldiers searching the palace never found.

Sources shown: Arenvald's Adventure — main scenario quest (4.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M502a** Lyse says Doma had Lord Hien ready to rule, but Ala Mhigo has no one like him. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "The Domans had Lord Hien ready and willing to take the throne, but we've got no one like that here."
  - **M502b** Theodoric, Ala Mhigo's last ruler, was called the mad king for good reason. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "Theodoric was our last ruler—and he wasn't called the mad king for nothing."
  - **M502e** Theodoric had everyone with a claim to the throne executed, his own family included. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "And so he ordered that every soul with a claim to the throne be executed—including his own family."
  - **M502f** Theodoric is said to have hoarded the wealth of the kinsmen he executed. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "[[King Theodoric]] is reputed to have hoarded the personal wealth of his executed kinsmen"
  - **M502g** Soldiers who searched the palace after the liberation found no treasure. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "But even after scouring every room from dawn till dusk, they uncovered not a single coin."
  - **M502h** Arenvald is set on you and Alphinaud finding the mad king's trove. *Arenvald's Adventure* (4.1, main): "Needless to say, Arenvald is determined that you should be the ones to uncover the mad king's trove."

</details>

**#503 only · main**
